endorsements.quote: Clinician-in-the-loop design must preserve human interpretive authority, support contestability, and enable contextual reintegration of outputs into broader developmental reasoning ( Amann et al., 2020 ; Sadeghi et al., 2024 ; Albahri et al., 2023 ).
Human review must include the ability to contest, revise, or reject algorithmic interpretations.

Future prototypes should include data dictionaries, model documentation, version control, audit trails, and, where appropriate, model cards or datasheets describing intended use, limitations, training data, validation status, uncertainty behavior, and known risks.

FIAP ® -Digital must be evaluated for differential performance across age, sex, language, socioeconomic context, race/ethnicity where appropriate, service access, geographic location, data availability, and communication profile.
Uncertainty should be visible at multiple levels: variable level, construct level, profile level, and longitudinal interpretation level.
The system should provide reason-giving outputs rather than labels alone.

Finally, implementation should proceed through staged testing: feasibility studies, micro-pilots, construct validation, prototype testing, longitudinal evaluation, cross-site replication, fairness assessment, and only later clinical translation.
Any future prototype must therefore be evaluated for usability, time burden, interpretability, and perceived usefulness.
FIAP ® -Digital should not generate autonomous diagnostic, prognostic, treatment, or service-allocation decisions.
Harmonization will therefore require structured variable definitions, data dictionaries, source documentation, and transparent mapping between observed indicators and FIAP ® constructs.
Outputs should be reviewed by clinicians or qualified researchers who can contextualize findings, consider alternative explanations, and identify limitations.

unlisted_practices: Collect only data necessary for the research question or validation stage (data minimization).
Do not enter identifiable participant data into external AI systems.
Separate identifying information from analytical data and store participant-level data securely with restricted access.
Match model complexity to the stage of validation and introduce advanced AI methods only when justified by sample size, data quality, and interpretability.
Explicitly flag low confidence rather than generating a deterministic profile when data are insufficient.
Design AI tools in tiers that rely on low-cost, accessible data first to avoid excluding under-resourced families.
Represent missingness with flags and completeness scores, and prioritize transparency over forced imputation.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual, hypothesis-and-theory framework paper proposing an AI architecture (FIAP-Digital) and validation roadmap rather than presenting an empirical study.
